source_interpretation.topic: Local base generation and uncertain oxidation
source_interpretation.text: Cathodic water reduction is proposed to produce hydroxide near the electrode, allowing Ce(III) hydrolysis to a hydroxide or hydrous oxide. The authors discuss subsequent oxidation by dissolved oxygen or electrogenerated hydrogen peroxide but explicitly say the Ce(III)-to-Ce(IV) mechanism is unresolved. Their mechanism is not a validated balanced reaction or measured intermediate structure.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Electrochemical synthesis discussion

source_interpretation.topic: Temperature controls crystallization independently of the imposed current
source_interpretation.text: At fixed cathodic current density, the authors treat the base-generation rate as constant while hydrolysis, condensation and crystallization accelerate with solution temperature. They interpret the larger crystallites at higher solution temperature accordingly; lower deposition current is a proposed direction, not a separately quantified series here.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 3 and discussion

source_interpretation.topic: Nanopowders improve densification more than onset temperature
source_interpretation.text: The source compares nanocrystalline powder with a purchased coarser comparator. It finds a large improvement in densification rate and completion temperature, while sintering onset moves only about 100 °C. A dense 1300 °C compact has much larger grains than the as-produced crystallites, so grain growth remains part of the tradeoff.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3–4, Sintering results, Figures6–8

source_interpretation.topic: Future directions are not demonstrated recipes
source_interpretation.text: Electrohydrothermal processing, doped powders and oxide films are discussed as future work. The paper does not provide products or recipes for them. The authors note that hydrogen evolution could complicate a hydrothermal implementation.
